name: Gemlik
title: Gemlik Ship Gauging: UTM for Car Carriers and Containers
description: Thickness gauging at Gemlik for car carriers, container ships and fertiliser bulk carriers: UTM of ramps, car decks, ballast tanks and holds during port calls.
h1: Ship Thickness Measurement at Gemlik, Bursa's Gulf Port
intro: Gemlik is Bursa's seaport, at the head of a sheltered gulf on the south-east side of the Sea of Marmara. Its quays are built around the automotive and manufacturing industry of the Bursa region, so pure car carriers, ro-ro ships and container ships call on regular schedules, and fertiliser and general cargo add bulk traffic. These scheduled calls suit planned gauging. Technicians travel from India to the ship, working alongside or by launch at the gulf anchorage.

highlights.p: Pure car and truck carriers load and discharge vehicles at the gulf's ro-ro berths. Ramps, hoistable decks and ballast tanks can be gauged between loading phases, with the sequence agreed with the chief officer.
Container ships and general cargo ships serve the Bursa industrial hinterland. Scheduled visits allow ballast tank, hatch cover and deck gauging within the terminal's permit rules.
The gulf's calm water makes launch work easier than on the open Marmara, so ships waiting for berths can take a longer programme in deck and ballast tank readings.

port.h: Gemlik and the gulf behind Bursa
p: The Gulf of Gemlik cuts into the south-eastern corner of the Sea of Marmara, and Gemlik town lies at its head, within reach of the city of Bursa and its industrial districts. Hills on both sides shelter the water, so the approach is more protected than the exposed shores of the central Marmara, and ships can lie at anchor in the gulf in conditions that would make launch transfers difficult elsewhere. The port grew up around Bursa's industry, and its terminals are mostly private facilities serving specific sectors.

Vehicle traffic is the signature trade. The Bursa region is a centre of Turkish car and component manufacturing, and finished vehicles leave the country, and imported vehicles arrive, through Gemlik's ro-ro and car terminals. Pure car and truck carriers are therefore regular callers, as are ro-ro ships carrying trailers. Container ships and feeders call at a modern container terminal, fertiliser and chemical cargoes move through their own berths, and liquid terminals take fuel and products. Bulk carriers and general cargo ships fill in the remaining berths, bringing steel, grain and project cargo.

For a superintendent, Gemlik's value is predictability. Vehicle carriers and container ships call on timetables, so an owner can fit a gauging visit into a call weeks ahead. The ships themselves have particular wear patterns: ramps and car decks suffer from vehicle traffic and wash-down, ballast tanks work hard to trim a high-sided ship, and hatch cover structures on container ships fatigue at corners. Gauging at Gemlik builds up a record over successive calls so that when the ship reaches a docking, the steel list is already drawn from measurements.

facilities.h: Where a ship can be gauged at Gemlik
p: At the vehicle terminals, access to a car carrier depends on the loading programme. Between vehicle movements, decks are cleared enough for readings on ramps, hoistable and fixed car decks, their supports and the adjacent side shell, while ballast tanks and cofferdams are entered from deck once certified. The team works deck by deck as the chief officer releases space, and does not block the ramps. At the container terminal the programme is similar to other box ships: ballast tanks, hatch covers, coamings and deck during cargo work, with items needing the ship empty held for a docking.

At the bulk and general cargo berths, holds are measured after discharge. Ships at the gulf anchorage can be boarded by launch arranged through the agent for deck, hatch and ballast tank gauging. There is no drydock for larger ships at Gemlik, so a ship needing a dry hull normally moves to Tuzla or the Yalova yards across the Marmara, and readings taken here go forward into the yard's steel estimate. The plan is laid out by compartment, so the yard planner can see at once which areas the readings flag.
list: Vehicle terminal berths — ramps, car decks, supports and ballast tanks on pure car and truck carriers between loading phases
Container terminal — ballast tanks, hatch covers, coamings and deck on container ships during scheduled calls
Fertiliser and chemical berths — holds, deck and ballast tanks on ships working corrosive cargoes
General cargo and bulk quays — hold frames, tank tops and coamings after discharge
Gemlik gulf anchorage — deck and ballast tank gauging on ships awaiting berths, reached by launch through the agent
Docking elsewhere on the Marmara — readings forwarded to a yard's steel estimate

context.h: Port state control, vetting and automotive supply chains
p: Ships at Gemlik are inspected under the Black Sea MoU and Mediterranean MoU regimes that Turkey belongs to, with the harbour master and the Ministry of Transport and Infrastructure acting for the state. Vehicle carriers are high-sided ships with large ballast capacity, and structural findings on ramps, ramp hinges and ballast tank plating can show up in deficiency records. Car manufacturers' logistics departments and their charterers tend to vet carriers closely, so owners keep thickness records up to date to show that the structure is sound.

Gemlik's trade is tied to the supply chains of the Bursa industrial region, which in turn depend on European markets. Vehicle carriers heading from here to EU ports must carry a valid Inventory of Hazardous Materials and report under the EU's carbon rules, and technical managers use measured thickness data to support those records and to plan dockings. Turkish yards in the Marmara can take a car carrier for a docking, but the ship's schedule is tight, so decisions about steel need to be made quickly once readings are in.

psc: Black Sea MoU and Mediterranean MoU

jobs.h: Typical thickness gauging jobs at Gemlik
jobs.p: Gemlik work fits around vehicle and container schedules. A superintendent identifies the ramps, decks or tanks that need numbers, we agree a plan with the terminal and the ship's officers, and the team uses the periods when those areas are free. Some calls are preparation for a docking, others respond to a charterer's question or a deficiency, and a few come from the sale of a car carrier. Results are returned by compartment.
list: Stern ramp, side ramp and hoistable deck gauging on a pure car and truck carrier during a vehicle loading call.
Ballast tank and cofferdam readings on a car carrier at the gulf anchorage, giving a docking steel list before the ship is booked in.
Hatch cover and coaming gauging on a container ship over repeated scheduled calls, tracking wastage at the corners.
Hold and deck gauging on a general cargo ship after fertiliser discharge, with coating condition noted.
Deck piping and ballast line readings on a ro-ro ship following a leak found in the pump room.
Pre-purchase gauging on a second-hand car carrier at the anchorage, with the buyer's adviser attending.

logistics: The team flies into Istanbul, usually Sabiha Gökçen Airport, and reaches Gemlik by road across the Osmangazi Bridge, with Bursa's airport an alternative for some domestic connections. The ship's agent arranges terminal passes, launches for the gulf anchorage and the ISPS formalities at the vehicle and container berths, and receives crew lists, certificates and equipment details beforehand. Indian technicians need a Turkish visa, so we begin the application once the call is nominated and keep the validity period flexible.

faqs.q: Can car carrier ramps and decks be gauged during loading?
faqs.a: Often yes, in the gaps between vehicle movements. We work deck by deck as the chief officer releases space, and we stay clear of ramps in use. Ballast tanks and cofferdams entered from deck can be gauged in parallel. The plan is agreed with the terminal and the ship's officers before boarding.

faqs.q: Is there a drydock at Gemlik?
faqs.a: Not for larger merchant ships. Ships that need a dry hull go to Tuzla, to the Yalova yards or to another Marmara yard. Readings taken here are reported by compartment so the yard can use them straight away as a steel estimate, which shortens planning once the ship is booked in.

faqs.q: How does the gulf anchorage compare with the open Marmara?
faqs.a: It is more sheltered, so launch transfers are usually easier and longer programmes are realistic. The ship may still be called to the berth at short notice, so we agree a priority list and take the most important readings first. The agent decides on the day whether the sea state is suitable.

faqs.q: Can container ship hatch covers be gauged between calls?
faqs.a: Yes, during a scheduled stop, within the terminal's permit conditions. Tops, coamings and corners are accessible between cargo operations, and readings over successive calls show whether wastage is progressing. Items that need the ship empty or the hull dry are noted for the next docking.

faqs.q: Can you check fertiliser holds after discharge?
faqs.a: Yes. Once the cargo is out and the crew has cleaned the holds to the point of safe entry, we gauge frames, tank tops and hopper plating, and record coating condition. Timing is planned around the next loading so the holds are returned to the ship in time.
